# Introduction 

## Performance Threshold Management API Specification

This document defines the REST API for managing performance thresholds. It includes the model definitions and all available operations necessary for creating, modifying, retrieving, and deleting performance thresholds and associated rules.

The Performance Threshold Management API enables systems to identify exceptional behavior in monitored performance indicators. It is designed as an additional layer on top of standard Performance Monitoring systems.

## Overview

Performance Threshold Management focuses on identifying and reacting to abnormal values in performance metrics. Applications that generate performance indicators (PM Producing Applications) are expected to:

- Set thresholds on those indicators
- Trigger alarms when thresholds are breached
- Send alarm clear events when the values return to normal ranges

This system enhances observability and automated responses to performance degradation or unusual behavior.

## Possible Actions

The API allows the following operations:

- Creating, retrieving, modifying, and deleting **threshold rules**
- Creating, retrieving, modifying, and deleting **thresholds**
- Creating, retrieving, modifying, and deleting **threshold jobs**

## Purpose

The Performance Thresholding API provides a standardized interface to Service and Resource Performance Management Systems. It enables manipulation of:

- Threshold rules
- Violation rules
- Exception rules

It supports:

- Alarms and notifications when exceptions occur
- Scheduling the evaluation of thresholds and violations

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Clients

Typical API consumers (clients) include:

- Resource Performance Monitoring Applications
- Resource Performance Analysis Applications

As part of the HIP (Hybrid Infrastructure Platform), this API is exposed for use by:

- Platform capability consumers
- Platform Capability Managers for capability delivery assurance

## Capabilities

The API supports the ability to define a **Threshold** as a collection of rules. These rules determine:

- When an alarm should be raised
- When an alarm should be cleared
- What severity level applies to each alarm

Each rule includes the expected fields to be set in the **Threshold Crossing Alarm (TCA)** that is triggered.

## Supported Operations

The API supports:

- Creation of Performance Thresholds
- Deletion of Performance Thresholds
- Querying of existing Performance Thresholds

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# Sample Use Cases 

## Overview

A Thresholding mechanism is a significant tool to identify exceptional behaviour at different management layers, at network level, service level and even customer level. It is assumed that a Performance Management system is deployed to collect and calculate measurements (e.g. Counters, KPIs, KQIs) that have significance to various departments of the Service Operator:

- Operations (e.g., Network uptime)
- Engineering (e.g., Packet loss rate)
- Marketing (e.g., Customer churn rate)
- Customer Care (e.g., Average call handling time)

Performance Management systems are sometimes limited to a specific domain or technology and sometimes much wider serving multiple domains, multiple technologies and multiple management layers.

In many typical scenarios, there is a need of management systems to get the information on exceptional behaviour as reflected in values of KPIs. This may be needed as a tool to identify lack of network resources (e.g. Bandwidth, CPU, transport links) to realize an insufficient Quality of Service or even bad customer experience.

As shown in the diagram below, a management system that requires the information on exceptional behaviour of KPIs is typically requesting this information from the Performance management system that collects the relevant counters or calculates the KPIs. Using the Threshold management system will define the threshold defines the threshold and whenever the threshold is crossed the Performance management system will send a threshold crossing alarm using the standard TM Forum Alarm management API. Other consequences (not just alarms) may also be defined in a textual format.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Threshold Definition Steps

A threshold is defined and executed in the target Performance management system in following steps:

1. Defining a threshold rule
2. Defining a threshold
3. Defining a threshold job that will execute the threshold with a scope of monitored objects (resources, services, and customers) at a specific schedule.

## Threshold Rule Types

The Threshold Rule is the heart of this interface. It allows to define logic that determines when to alert on exceptional values of KPIs and on return to normal conditions. The Thresholding API supports two kinds of thresholds:

- Simple Thresholds – defined explicitly by a set of attributes
- Threshold algorithms – a case where the threshold is actually an algorithm to be executed with parameters

The simple threshold rules provide support for simple cases such as comparing a value of a KPI to a constant, but it can also support more interesting options such as checking ranges of values or counting events in a particular time interval and more.

It is also possible to define an action that will be triggered when a threshold rule is valid. In most cases the action will be raising or clearing a threshold crossing alarm (using the Alarm management interface). In other cases a generic kind of an action, described by a text or a URL can be defined.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The Threshold resource packs a set of threshold rules to single logic (with an "OR" condition among them) such that hysteresis or multi-range thresholds can be supported.

## Threshold Job

The Threshold Job is the operational entity responsible for executing a threshold, which consists of a set of threshold rules. It evaluates a collection of monitored objects—such as resources, services, and customers—at specific intervals as determined by the job’s schedule. The job is designed to trigger alerts or actions when certain conditions or thresholds are met, ensuring that system performance, service levels, or other criteria are continuously monitored.

As part of defining a Threshold Job, two key elements are specified:

1. Scope of Monitored Objects:

```
This defines the set of resources, services, and customers that will be
monitored by the job. The monitored objects are subject to threshold evaluationsbased on the rules set during job configuration.
```

2. Schedule:

```
A specific schedule is set for when the threshold job will run and evaluate thedefined thresholds. This schedule could be based on fixed intervals (e.g.,
hourly, daily) or specific times.
```

## Execution States

Each Threshold Job has an associated Execution State, which represents the status or condition of the job at any given time during its lifecycle. The possible execution states for a threshold job are as follows:

- Active:

```
The job is currently active and running according to its schedule. This stateindicates that the job is ongoing and performing the threshold checks.
```

- Suspended:

```
The job has been suspended either manually or due to certain conditions thattemporarily stop its execution. The job is not executing during this state, butit can be resumed later.
```

- Failed:

```
The job encountered an error during its execution, causing it to fail. The
failure might result from an issue with the job itself (e.g., misconfiguration,
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

```
 system failure) or from the monitored objects not meeting the required
thresholds. The job is not active during this state.
```

- Completed:

```
The job has successfully completed its execution. All the threshold checks havebeen performed, and the job has finished its task. It is no longer active, butit has successfully completed its intended work.
```

## State Machine

A state machine diagram illustrates how the threshold job transitions through these execution states, depending on events such as job initiation, error occurrence, or completion of tasks. The diagram would typically show transitions between Active, Suspended, Failed, and Completed states in response to triggers like job start, error detection, or successful completion.

# Support of polymorphism and extension patterns

## Overview

Support for polymorphic collections, types, and schema-based extensions is provided through a set of generic meta-attributes, described below. Polymorphism in collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities—for example, the rule types SimpleThresholdRule and AlgorithmThresholdRule inheriting properties from a common base entity that is ThresholdRule.

Generic support of polymorphism and pattern extensions is described in the TMF API Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).

## Meta-Attributes

The @type attribute provides a way to represent the actual class type of an entity. For example, within a list of Characteristic instances some may be instances of StringCharacteristic where other could be instances of IntegerCharacteristic. The @type gives this information. All resources and sub-resources of this API have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.

The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance an PerformanceMeasurementRef object) to explicitly denote the actual entity type of the referred class. Notice that in reference entities the @type, when used, denotes the class type of the reference itself, such as PerformanceMeasurementRef, and not the class type of the referred object. However since reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in reference objects.

The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.

The @baseType attribute gives a way to provide explicitly the base of class of a given resource that has been extended.

### ThresholdJob resource

The Threshold Job is the operational entity to execute a threshold (a set of threshold rules). As part of the definition of a Threshold Job, a scope of monitored objects is provided and a schedule for the threshold evaluation is determined.

### Resource model

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

_Figure 4 - ThresholdJob_

**Field descriptions**

**ThresholdJob fields**

| adminState | An AdminStateEnum. Enumeration of administrative states of aresource. Possible values indicate whether the resource islocked, unlocked, or shutting down. ENUMERATED with values:\* LOCKED\* UNLOCKED\* SHUTTING\_DOWN |
| --- | --- |
| creationDate | A DateTime. Timestamp indicating when the Threshold Job wasoriginally created in the Performance Management system. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| executionState | A String. The current runtime state of the Threshold Job.Supported states: 'Active' - The job is currently active andexecuting threshold evaluation. 'Suspended' - The job istemporarily stopped but can be resumed. 'Failed' - The jobstopped due to a failure. 'Completed' - The job has finished itsexecution successfully and is no longer active. |
| --- | --- |
| granularity | A String. Defines the evaluation granularity of the Threshold Job(e.g., G\_5MN, G\_15MN, G\_30MN, G\_1H). It specifies theperiodic time interval at which KPIs are assessed againstthreshold rules. |
| href | A String. Hyperlink reference. |
| id | A String. Unique identifier. |
| jobPriority | An Integer32. Relative priority level assigned to the ThresholdJob. Higher priority jobs may be executed or scheduled ahead oflower priority jobs. |
| lastUpdate | A DateTime. Timestamp of the most recent update ormodification to the Threshold Job definition. |
| monitoredObjectsCriteria | A MonitoredObjectsCriteria. Criteria that define the scope ofmonitored objects (resources, services, or customers) to whichthe Threshold Job applies. |
| performanceThreshold | A ThresholdRef. |
| scheduleDefinition | A ScheduleDefinition. The schedule definition for running jobs. |
| trackingRecord | A String. Optional field to store tracking or correlation informationrelated to the Threshold Job (e.g., audit trails, externalreferences, or operator notes). |
| @baseType | A String. When sub-classing, this defines the super-class. |
| @schemaLocation | A String. A URI to a JSON-Schema file that defines additionalattributes and relationships. |
| @type | A String. When sub-classing, this defines the sub-classExtensible name. |

## Notification Resource Models

10 notifications are defined for this API.

Notifications related to Threshold:

- Create Event
- Delete Event
- Attribute Value Change Event

Notifications related to ThresholdRule:

- Create Event
- Delete Event
- Attribute Value Change Event

Notifications related to ThresholdJob:

- Create Event
- Delete Event
- Attribute Value Change Event
- State Change Event

The notification structure for all notifications in this API follow the pattern depicted by the figure below. A notification event resource (depicted by "SpecificEvent" placeholder) is a sub class of a generic Event structure containing at least an id of the event occurrence (eventId), an event timestamp (eventTime), and the name of the resource (eventType). This notification structure owns an event payload structure ("SpecificEventPayload" placeholder) linked to the resource concerned by the notification using the resource name as access field ("resourceName" placeholder).

# API OPERATIONS 

## Uniform Contract

Remember the following Uniform Contract:

| Operation on Entities | Uniform API Operation | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query Entities | GET Resource | GET must be used to retrieve arepresentation of a resource. |
| Create Entity | POST Resource | POST must be used to create anew resource |
| Partial Update of an Entity | PATCH Resource | PATCH must be used to partiallyupdate a resource |
| Remove an Entity | DELETE Resource | DELETE must be used toremove a resource |
| Execute an Action on an Entity | POST on TASK Resource | POST must be used to executeTask Resources |
| Other Request Methods | POST on TASK Resource | GET and POST must not beused to tunnel other requestmethods. |

## Filtering and Attribute Selection

Filtering and attribute selection rules are described in the TMF REST Design Guidelines.

Notifications are also described in a subsequent section.

## Available Operations

## Operations on Threshold

### List or find Threshold objects

```
GET /threshold?fields=…
```

**Description**

This operation list Threshold entities. Attribute selection is enabled for all first level attributes. Filtering may be available depending on the compliance level supported by an implementation.

### Updates partially a Threshold

### PATCH /threshold/{id}?fields=…

### Description

This operation allows partial updates of a Threshold entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) [html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub-resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

### Patchable and Non Patchable Attributes

| description |  |
| href |  |
| id |  |
| name |  |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| **Non Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| thresholdRule |  |
| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |

### Updates partially a ThresholdRule

### PATCH /thresholdRule/{id}?fields=…

### Description

This operation allows partial updates of a ThresholdRule entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) [html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub-resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

### Updates partially a ThresholdJob

### PATCH /thresholdJob/{id}?fields=…

### Description

This operation allows partial updates of a ThresholdJob entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) [html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub-resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

| id |  |

| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| --- | --- |
| adminState |  |
| creationDate |  |
| executionState |  |
| granularity |  |
| jobPriority |  |
| lastUpdate |  |

| performanceThreshold |  |

# API NOTIFICATIONS 

For every single of operation on the entities use the following templates and provide sample REST notification POST calls.

It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in the REST Guidelines reproduced below.

## Register listener

**POST /hub**

**Description**

Sets the communication endpoint address the service instance must use to deliver information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.

**Request**

```
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
```

**Response**

```
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42
{
    "id":"42",
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com",    "query":""
}
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Unregister listener

**DELETE /hub/{id}**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.

**Request**

```
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
```

**Response**

```
204
```

## Publish Event to listener

**POST /client/listener**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.

Provides to a registered listener the description of the event that was raised. The /client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 201 if the service is able to set the configuration.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a notification received by the listener. In this example “EVENT TYPE” should be replaced by one of the notification types supported by this API (see Notification resources Models section) and EVENT BODY refers to the data structure of the given notification type.

**Request**

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

```
POST /client/listener
Accept: application/json
{
    "event": {
        EVENT BODY    },
    "eventType": "EVENT_TYPE"
}
```

**Response**

```
201
```

For detailed examples on the general TM Forum notification mechanism, see the TMF REST Design Guidelines.
